platforms.name: Android
platforms.text: Open the app and your phone is an Xbox controller. Pair it once from the computer's Bluetooth settings as "Xbox Wireless Controller" — nothing to install on the computer — and games, Steam and browser cloud gaming see a standard Xbox pad, with rumble. Matte-black controls with real button feel: a crisp click on every press, taps that are never lost however fast, and a little forgiveness at the edge of each button. Seven layouts you can move and resize, gyro aim, tilt steering, turbo, Controller Lock. No internet permission, no account, no ads. Open the file on your phone and allow installing from your browser when Android asks. Updates earlier versions in place; after updating, turn the computer's Bluetooth off and on once.
platforms.tested: This exact file (signed release 0.5.0) was installed over 0.4.0 on a realme 12 5G (Android 16), opened straight into the controller and reconnected to a MacBook Air (macOS 27.0.1) as "Xbox Wireless Controller". Read through Apple's GameController framework, every control sent only itself (20/20) — A, B, X, Y, bumpers, triggers, View, Menu, stick clicks, the D-pad four ways and both sticks — a touch between Y and B sent nothing, Guide opened the Mac's Games overlay as a real Xbox pad does, and a game-style rumble vibrated the phone.
